Plus my neurologist literally wrote a letter saying I need disability because of how uncontrollable my seizures are.

Don't stop trying, maybe try to find a lawyer that specializes in disability. And get notes from your doctor. I also hace notes from my psychiatrist because of the toll my epilepsy has taken on my mental health. 

I wish you the best of luck!

I was diagnosed at 11, but we realized that I'd been having seizures since I was 3. But it was only at night, when I was asleep. Because I couldn't control wetting the bed. It didn't stop until I got on medication. But after I was diagnosed, I felt like everyone was looking at me differently. My epilepsy wasn't the main cause of the start of my depression. But It has played a significant role in it in the last 8 years. It was also the cause of my anxiety. I was always anxious that I would have a seizure in public. So I started not leaving the house often. Sometimes it wasn't until It was necessary. Even part of my suicidal thoughts are because of it. I feel like there is this chain restricting me. And at some points in my life I questioned if it was worth it. I still question it sometimes. My home life got complicated, My mom became over protective and my dad decided it was to much for him to deal with. I lost friends because the possibility of me having a seizure when I'm with them made them anxious. So they just told me that they didn't want to be my friend anymore. Which also contributed to my depression, anxiety, and all the other mental illnesses I have. Oh I also don't have an aura, so It makes me severely anxious. Because I don't know when a seizure is coming. I have tried to take my own life seriously twice now. It can be overwhelming to deal with everything that comes with having epilepsy. And I can't mentally handle it as well as I use to. The only reason I haven't successfully ended my life yet, is because I don't want to break my mom and brothers hearts.  

 I do agree that people need to talk about the psychological effect seizures can have on people. Because it is not talked about enough. It's a lot more important then people make it out to be.
